{{Short description|British physicist (1924–2006)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2023}}[[File:Gulyaev Hogarth 1963 postcard 02.jpg|thumb|Postcard from [[Yuri Gulyayev (physicist)|Yuri Gulyayev]] to Hogarth, 16 December 1963]]
'''Cyril Alfred Hogarth''' (22 January 1924 – 6 November 2006)<ref name="Times obit" /> was a British physicist and chairman of [[South Bucks District Council]].<ref name="Bucks Free Press obit" /> A pioneer in the field of [[oxide]] semiconductors,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Ray |first=Asim |date=2006 |title=Special Issue on oxides in electronics, dedicated to Cyril Hogarth |url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s10854-006-0049-5.pdf |journal=Journal of Materials Science: Materials in Electronics |volume=17 |issue=9 |pages=647–649 |doi=10.1007/s10854-006-0049-5 |s2cid=136879133 |via=[[EBSCOHost]]}}</ref> he was a professor, head of the physics department, and administrator at [[Brunel University London]], where he worked for 31 years.<ref name="Journal of Materials Science obit">{{cite journal |last1=Carter |first1=C Barry |date=1 April 2007 |title=Professor Cyril A Hogarth |journal=Journal of Materials Science |volume=42 |issue=8 |page=2537 |doi=10.1007/s10853-006-1471-z |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10853-006-1471-z |access-date=10 June 2023|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Times obit">{{cite news |title=Professor C.A. Hogarth |url=https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/professor-ca-hogarth-cnkdt869jk3 |access-date=10 June 2023 |work=[[The Times]] |date=15 January 2007}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Hogarth was born in 1924, and grew up in [[Tottenham]], north London.<ref name="Times obit" /> He was educated at [[Tottenham County School]].<ref name="Times obit" /> Hogarth earned a degree from the [[University of London]].<ref name="Times obit" /><ref name="Bucks Free Press obit" /> 

In 1948, he received a PhD from [[Queen Mary University of London]],<ref name="Journal of Materials Science obit" /> studying with Professor J. P. Andrews.<ref name=":0" /> That year, Hogarth's theoretical solution for determining the dependence of thermoelectric power of [[cadmium oxide]] on ambient oxygen pressure was published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' and in ''[[Philosophical Magazine]]''.<ref name=":0" /> He later received a [[Doctor of Science|doctor of science]] degree in 1977.<ref name=":0" /> 

== Career ==
From 1943 to 1946, Hogarth worked on naval radar and countermeasures in the UK, Canada, the US and the Arctic.<ref name="Journal of Materials Science obit" /> After earning his PhD, he lectured at [[Chelsea College of Science and Technology]] and the [[University of Reading]], before spending some years at the [[Royal Radar Establishment]].<ref name="Journal of Materials Science obit" />

Hogarth was "closely involved" in the founding of [[Brunel University London]] from 1958, its first professor of physics, head of its physics department, and its pro vice-chancellor for a year in 1980.<ref name="Times obit"/><ref name="Journal of Materials Science obit"/><ref name="Bucks Free Press obit">{{cite news |last1=Brunetti |first1=Nic |title=World-renowned physicist dies |url=https://www.bucksfreepress.co.uk/news/1015526.world-renowned-physicist-dies/ |access-date=10 June 2023 |work=Bucks Free Press |date=10 November 2006}}</ref>

In 1969, Hogarth was elected as vice-president of the [[Institute of Physics]] and the Physical Society.<ref name="Physics Today">{{cite web |title=Report Suggests Regional Problem‐Solving Centers |url=https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article-abstract/22/10/69/398181/Report-Suggests-Regional-Problem-Solving-Centers?redirectedFrom=fulltext |website=Physics Today |access-date=10 June 2023}}</ref> 

Hogarth retired from Brunel University in 1989, but continued his research and published articles regularly through the mid-1990s.<ref name="Journal of Materials Science obit" /> In 1990 and 1991 alone, he published 17 and 13 articles, respectively, in the ''Journal of Materials Science''.<ref name="Journal of Materials Science obit" /> In addition to semiconductors, his research focused on materials and their properties.<ref name="Journal of Materials Science obit" />

== Personal life and death ==
In 1951, Cyril married Dr Audrey Hogarth (1926 – 2010), who had a doctorate in dairy bacteriology from [[Reading University]].<ref name="Audrey Hogarth obit">{{cite news |last1=Dunhill |first1=Lawrence |title=Community figure, Audrey Hogarth, dies aged 83 |url=https://www.bucksfreepress.co.uk/news/8170177.community-figure-audrey-hogarth-dies-aged-83/ |access-date=10 June 2023 |work=Bucks Free Press |date=17 May 2010}}</ref> The Hogarths lived in [[Gerrards Cross]], where Audrey served as a magistrate for 29 years.<ref name="Audrey Hogarth obit" /> They had three children together: Celia Stuart-Lee, a teacher; Adrian Hogarth, a lawyer; and Yvonne, who died in 1994.<ref name="Audrey Hogarth obit"/>

Cyril Hogarth was chairman of the Gerrards Cross [[Conservative Association]] and served as a district councillor in South Bucks for 20 years.<ref name="Bucks Free Press obit" /> He died on 6 November 2006, immediately after a parish council meeting, most likely from a heart attack, at the age of 82.<ref name="Bucks Free Press obit" />

* Alani, SKJ; Hogarth, CA; Elmalawany, RA (1985). ''Journal of Materials Science'' '''20'''(2):661.
* Anastasiadis, C; Triantis, D; Hogarth, CA (2007). "Comments on the phenomena underlying pressure stimulated currents (PSC) in dielectric rock materials". ''Journal of Materials Science'' '''42'''.
* Khan, MN; Harani, R; Ahmed, MM; Hogarth, CA (1985). ''Journal of Materials Science'' '''20'''(6):2207.
